messages:
sara: Hey team — quick Q. Baby due ~6 weeks. I'm mid-performance-cycle and there’s an internal interview for a lateral transfer scheduled next Wednesday. How does taking parental leave affect the review timeline, promo/bonus eligibility, and the interview? Do I need to pause the hiring process? cc @mike-manager @people-ops

lisa-hr: Congrats, Sara! :tada: Short answers: your review still happens and compensation decisions are not automatically disqualified by leave. We do a couple of adjustments depending on timing — details below. Please file the leave request first so we have official dates.

mike-manager: From a manager side I can move the interview or keep it depending on what you prefer. We usually don’t cancel reviews — I can run calibration notes with your work up to the review cutoff. If you want the interview paused, @jamie-recruiter can put the loop on hold.

jamie-recruiter: Can pause, no problem. If Sara prefers, we can reschedule to after her return window. If the role needs coverage we can widen the pool and do async screeners. Which approach do you want, @sara?

sara: Thanks — I’d prefer not to lose momentum on the transfer, but also don’t want to interview while away. Could we do the screening step now (take-home) and leave on-site/comp loop until I’m back?

lisa-hr: That’s a great compromise and we support it. Screening tasks are fine. For final interview loops, managers/teams typically either schedule immediately before leave or after return. For the review: managers submit their assessment based on the review period work. If a decision (raise/bonus/promo) is deferred because of leave timing, we document the rationale and aim to make retroactive adjustments if warranted.

people-ops: Note on compensation/bonus: full eligibility is based on time on payroll during the performance year. If your leave is paid leave under our parental policy, you remain eligible for prorated bonus and equity vesting continues as normal. For any special top-ups (salary continuation beyond statutory leave), we handle those as payroll entries once leave is approved.

payroll-bot: Reminder: please upload your estimated leave dates and any medical documentation to the HR portal (https://hr.redwood.example/leave) so payroll can calculate top-ups and benefits. Deadline to avoid payroll lag: 2 pay-cycles before start date.

mike-manager: I’ll also add a short handoff doc for your projects and set up interim owners. Sara, if you want, we can run a short review sync this week so your contributions are captured before you step out.

sara: That would be super helpful — thanks. How formal is the handoff? I can do 1 pager + runbook.

lisa-hr: 1-pager + ownership table is ideal. Also please indicate any performance goals you want considered for the review; managers can add contextual notes in the review form. If there’s a promotion decision dependent on a post-leave interview, we’ll note a conditional timeline in the review doc.

jamie-recruiter: I’ve paused booking the final loop for now and sent the take-home exercise. I’ll re-open scheduling when you give us a return window.

sara: Perfect. Filing the leave request now. Appreciate everyone moving so fast. :)

people-ops: Thanks — after you submit, reply here with the HR case ID and we’ll confirm payroll/top-up estimates and whether any documents are missing. We’ll also flag the performance window for calibration.

payroll-bot: Payroll task created: case 472319. Expected top-up estimate email within 3 business days after docs are complete.
